title: Geological Collections Glossary
description: Terms and definitions supporting the Geological Collections Conceptual Data Model (GCDM), an ontologically grounded conceptual data model for geologic specimen collections. Terms are drawn from the Terms subsections of the GCDM manuscript and cover data modeling and ontology, compound specimens, names and classification systems, stratigraphy, geologic age, and geologic settings and sampling events.
scopeNote: Covers the concepts required to interpret and implement the GCDM: data-modeling and ontology vocabulary, the compound specimen construct and its parts, names and classification systems, stratigraphic units, geologic age (relative and chronometric), and geologic settings and sampling events. Definitions are either reproduced from the cited standard or reference work, adapted from it, or authored for the GCDM; the provenance of each definition is recorded per term. Domain-specific classification values (e.g., individual Dana or Nickel-Strunz classes) are out of scope and are maintained in the GCDM Master Dictionary.
changeNote: 2026-07-30: Initial release. 105 terms extracted from the Terms subsections (§2.1, §3.1, §4.1, §5.1, §6.1, §7.1) of GCDM manuscript version 2026-07-27, with 44 cited sources resolved against the manuscript bibliography.
historyNote: This glossary was created as part of the GeoSpecify and SwissCollNet programs. The terms and definitions are intended to accompany an upcoming publication Geological Collections Conceptual Data Model (GCDM)

terms.label: Concept
terms.definition: A unit of knowledge created by a unique combination of characteristics.

terms.label: Conceptual Model
terms.definition: An abstract model or representation of data for a particular domain or field of study, independent of any specific software or information system.

terms.label: Data Model
terms.definition: Graphical and/or lexical representation of data, specifying their properties, structure, and interrelationships.

terms.label: Identifier
terms.definition: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.

terms.label: Logical Data Model
terms.definition: A data model that includes all entities and the relationships among them based on the structures identified in a conceptual data model and that specifies all attributes for each entity.

terms.label: Model
terms.definition: A simplified representation or abstraction of a system, process, or concept.

terms.label: Ontology
terms.definition: Specification of concrete or abstract things and the relationships among them in a prescribed domain of knowledge.

terms.label: Physical Data Model
terms.definition: A technical representation detailing how data is physically organized and constrained within a database system, focusing on tables, columns, and constraints rather than entities and attributes.

terms.label: Agent
terms.definition: An agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.

terms.label: Activity
terms.definition: Something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities; it may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.

terms.label: Collection Object
terms.definition: A physical object that belongs to a museum collection.

terms.label: Compound Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object comprised of one or more discernible parts, called specimen parts, unified by physical attachment. The object's identity is determined by its specimen parts, which are distinguished from one another within a specific context.
terms.scopeNote: Central construct of the GCDM. Contrast with Simple Specimen, which carries a single determination and no discernible parts. See GCDM section 3.2.

terms.label: Compound Specimen Model
terms.definition: A conceptual data model in which a single physical object, a compound specimen, is composed of and defined by its specimen parts.

terms.label: Specimen Part
terms.definition: A physically discernible, proximal portion of a compound specimen that carries a single determination and belongs to a single material category, distinguished from the rest of the parent specimen by its physical and chemical exclusivity.
terms.scopeNote: The unit of determination in the GCDM. Each Specimen Part carries exactly one determination and belongs to exactly one Material Category. See GCDM section 3.3.

terms.label: Specimen Part Proportion
terms.definition: Refers to the qualitative or quantitative representation of the abundance of a Specimen Part within a parent Compound Specimen.
terms.scopeNote: May be recorded qualitatively (e.g. dominant, subordinate, trace) or quantitatively (e.g. percentage). See GCDM section 3.3.2.

terms.label: Specimen Part Relation
terms.definition: A described uni-directional association between two specimen parts, a source and target, within the scope of the parent compound specimen. A relation is defined from the perspective of the source specimen part and described using a relation predicate.
terms.scopeNote: Directed from source part to target part and scoped to the parent Compound Specimen. See GCDM section 3.5.

terms.label: Specimen Part Role
terms.definition: Specifies the relationship between a Specimen Part and its parent compound specimen. Roles are dependent upon both the part and parent object. For instance, a rock (material category) within the parent specimen plays the role of clast and is dependent on both the specimen part and the parent specimen for its existence.
terms.scopeNote: Roles are contextual: the same material plays different roles depending on the parent object. See GCDM section 3.3.2.

terms.label: Material Category
terms.definition: A value from a top-level, generalized categorization scheme for geologic materials, in which each geologic material, a Compound Specimen or a Specimen Part, belongs to one and only one Material Category. For any given collection, the set of Material Categories should comprehensively account for all parts found across every specimen in that collection.
terms.scopeNote: The set of Material Categories used by a collection should be mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive for that collection.

terms.label: Determination
terms.definition: The identity of a specimen represented by a name based on formal criteria evaluated by a domain expert. In biological collections, the determination is represented by a taxonomic classification, primarily a genus and species (e.g., Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii). In the geosciences domain, examples of determination include Almandine, Granite, and Plantae.
terms.example: Almandine; Granite; Plantae; (biological analogues) Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii

terms.label: Geologic Material
terms.definition: An amount of matter primarily (dominantly) having parts created by geologic processes and can include minor parts that are not of geologic origin, such as organic material, and can be solid, fluid, or a mix.

terms.label: Geologic Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object comprised, in part, of geologic material.

terms.label: Material Entity
terms.definition: A material entity is an entity that exists in full during the length of time of its existence, persists through this time while maintaining its identity, and has no temporal parts.

terms.label: Object
terms.definition: An object is a maximal causally unified material entity, meaning b is a material entity which is such that its material parts are tied together in such a way that, in environments typical for entities of the type in question.

terms.label: Relation Predicate
terms.definition: Describes the nature of the relationship between two specimen parts within the scope of a compound specimen.

terms.label: Simple Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object identified by a single determination without discernible parts.

terms.label: Simple Specimen Model
terms.definition: The conceptual model for the digital representation of physical specimens where each entity is characterized by one and only one determination without any discernible parts.

terms.label: Alternate Name
terms.definition: An alternate lexical label to the preferred term for an entity.

terms.label: Authoritative Name
terms.definition: A name sanctioned by an authority based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature.

terms.label: Authority
terms.definition: Identifies the entity responsible for assigning and maintaining a formalized classification system.

terms.label: Classification
terms.definition: Activity involving grouping similar or related things together; separating dissimilar or unrelated things; and arranging the resulting groups in a logical and helpful sequence.

terms.label: Classification Code
terms.definition: Encoded classification of an object represented by a graphical symbol that conforms to an encoding scheme defined as part of the classification scheme.

terms.label: Classification Family
terms.definition: A grouping of related classification series (skos:Collection); e.g., all mineral classifications.
terms.scopeNote: Modeled as skos:Collection. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

terms.label: Classification Item
terms.definition: A single node of a classification scheme, one concept or named entry, modeled as a skos:Concept, to which a Specimen Part is classified.
terms.scopeNote: Modeled as skos:Concept. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

terms.label: Classification Item Relation
terms.definition: A reified, directed parent–child edge between two Classification Items that constitutes the hierarchy, typed by skos:broader/skos:narrower.
terms.scopeNote: Reified edge typed by skos:broader / skos:narrower. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

terms.label: Classification Level
terms.definition: A stratified tier comprised of nodes with a shared level of granularity in a hierarchy.

terms.label: Classification Name
terms.definition: A formalized name belonging to a classification system maintained by an authoritative body.

terms.label: Classification Rank
terms.definition: An identifier assigned to a classification level commonly expressed using a numeric identifier or lexical label.

terms.label: Classification Rank Relation
terms.definition: A reified ordering relation between two Classification Ranks, present only for ranked schemes.
terms.scopeNote: Present only for ranked schemes. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

terms.label: Classification Scheme
terms.definition: A method of organization according to a set of pre-established principles, usually characterized by a notation system and a hierarchical structure of relationships among the entities. This standard defines the structure and organization of a classification system, including its hierarchical ranks.

terms.label: Classification Series
terms.definition: The time-ordered set of successive versions of one classification (skos:OrderedCollection); e.g., the editions of Dana.
terms.scopeNote: Modeled as skos:OrderedCollection. See GCDM section 4.5.3.
terms.example: The successive editions of the Dana classification

terms.label: Classification System
terms.definition: A terminological resource that has characteristics of mutual exclusiveness and exhaustiveness to aggregate data to a pre-prescribed level of specialization for a specific purpose. Extends the classification scheme concept to include the values used to populate a classification scheme.

terms.label: Classification Term
terms.definition: A single concept in a classification system or scheme at any hierarchical level.

terms.label: Classification Version
terms.definition: A versioned instance of a classification scheme.

terms.label: Confirmation Protocol
terms.definition: The procedure by which a Name is verified or confirmed for a specimen.
terms.scopeNote: Carried by the determinedBy relation in GCDM Figure 10.

terms.label: Depth
terms.definition: The numeric distance of a nested level from the root of a hierarchy in a stratified classification scheme.

terms.label: Hierarchy
terms.definition: Concept system in which all concepts are related in hierarchical relations that form a partial ordering.

terms.label: Identification
terms.definition: The process of recognizing an entity in a particular domain as distinct from other entities.

terms.label: Linnaean Taxonomy
terms.definition: A classification system for grouping both living and extinct organisms, governed by the relevant nomenclatural codes (the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature for animals; the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants). Generally, the parent-child relationships in the Linnaean hierarchy represent the lineage evolution between species.
terms.scopeNote: Governed by the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature for animals and the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants.

terms.label: Monohierarchy
terms.definition: Hierarchical arrangement of concepts in a classification scheme in which each concept can have only one broader concept at the level immediately above.

terms.label: Name
terms.definition: The primary means of identification of objects and concepts for humans.

terms.label: Name Type
terms.definition: The category of a Name, Specimen, Authoritative, or Alternate, assigned through the hasType relation.
terms.scopeNote: Assigned through the hasType relation in GCDM Figure 10.

terms.label: Naming Authority
terms.definition: A registration authority that allocates names according to specified rules.

terms.label: Nomenclature Status
terms.definition: The standing of a Name within its nomenclatural system (e.g., approved, superseded), recorded through the hasStatus relation.
terms.scopeNote: Recorded through the hasStatus relation in GCDM Figure 10.

terms.label: Specimen Name
terms.definition: Refers to any name assigned to a specimen at the object level (before atomization into specimen parts). Specimen names are often written as compound terms, a concatenation of multiple informal and formal identifiers.
terms.scopeNote: Applies at the object level, before atomization into specimen parts; often a concatenation of informal and formal identifiers.

terms.label: Value Set
terms.definition: The range of values used to populate a classification scheme (or classification scheme variant).

terms.label: Biostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Geologic units defined or characterized on the basis of their contained fossils. Biostratigraphic units exist only where the particular diagnostic feature or attribute on which they are based has been identified.

terms.label: Chronostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Bodies of rocks, layered or unlayered, that are defined between specified stratigraphic horizons which represent specified intervals of geologic time.

terms.label: Geologic Unit
terms.definition: A body of rock that persists through time, forming a discrete and definable unit. Geologic units are identified by their geometric, compositional, and internal structural characteristics, as well as their spatio-temporal relations with other rock bodies.

terms.label: Geologic Unit Type
terms.definition: A scheme that specifies concepts used to categorize types of geologic units. Unit types are differentiated based on their defining composition, temporal context, or other physical properties.
terms.example: Lithostratigraphic; Chronostratigraphic; Biostratigraphic; Magnetostratigraphic; Tectonostratigraphic; Lithodemic

terms.label: Law of Superposition
terms.definition: A general law upon which all geologic chronology is based, where younger lithostratigraphic units lie atop older lithostratigraphic units.

terms.label: Lithodemic Unit
terms.definition: A defined body of predominantly intrusive, highly deformed, and (or) highly metamorphosed rock, distinguished and delimited based on rock characteristics.

terms.label: Lithology
terms.definition: (a) The description of rocks, especially in hand specimens and outcrops, based on characteristics such as color, mineralogic composition, and grain size. (b) The physical character of a rock.

terms.label: Lithostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: A defined body of sedimentary, extrusive igneous, metasedimentary, or metavolcanic strata that is distinguished and delimited based on lithic characteristics and stratigraphic position.

terms.label: Magnetostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Bodies of rock strata unified by similar magnetic characteristics which allow them to be differentiated from adjacent strata.

terms.label: Stratigraphy
terms.definition: The description of all rock bodies forming the Earth's crust and their organization into distinctive, useful, mappable units based on their inherent properties or attributes in order to establish their distribution and relationship in space and their succession in time, and to interpret geologic history.

terms.label: Tectonostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Geologic unit defined on basis of structural or deformation features, mutual relations, origin or historical evolution. Contained material may be igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.

terms.label: Geochronologic Boundary
terms.definition: Temporal boundaries defined with reference to some geologic evidence such as, for instance, fossil appearance/disappearance or significant change in local rock lithology.

terms.label: Geochronologic Era
terms.definition: A named interval of geologic time of any rank, used to express a Relative Age as a bounded ordinal interval.
terms.scopeNote: Used to express a Relative Age as a bounded ordinal interval. See GCDM Figure 22a.

terms.label: Geochronologic Interpretation
terms.definition: An interpretation made by a geologist of the age of a specimen made by statistical analysis of a single collection of observations. A specimen may have multiple geochronological interpretations made on it, each related to a different observation collection.

terms.label: Geochronologic Rank
terms.definition: The hierarchical level of a Geochronologic Era, Eon, Era, Period, Epoch, Age, carried through the hasRank relation.
terms.scopeNote: Carried through the hasRank relation in GCDM Figure 22a.

terms.label: Geochronologic Unit
terms.definition: A proper temporal interval that is a named, ranked subdivision of geologic time within a hierarchical ordinal temporal reference system, whose bounding instants are fixed either by designated reference points in the stratigraphic record or by assigned numerical ages, and which is the temporal counterpart of the chronostratigraphic unit of corresponding rank.
terms.scopeNote: Time, not rock. The material counterpart is a chronostratigraphic unit bearing the same proper name. Numerical ages are calibrations of the bounding instants, not part of the unit's identity.

terms.label: Geochronology
terms.definition: The science of determining absolute ages of geologic events and Earth materials. The primary technique utilizes radioactive isotopes and the production and accumulation of radiogenic daughter isotopes naturally present on Earth. It can be applied to various samples, including rocks, minerals, and biological materials.

terms.label: Geologic Event
terms.definition: An identifiable event during which one or more geologic processes act to modify geologic entities.

terms.label: Geologic Process
terms.definition: A natural process that affects the geologic record by acting upon one geologic entity to produce another geologic entity at a later time.

terms.label: Geologic Timescale
terms.definition: A temporal reference system that subdivides all the time since Earth formed into named intervals (units) of abstract time and subdivides all the rocks formed since Earth formed into the successions of rock formed during each particular interval of time.

terms.label: Chronometric Age
terms.definition: The age of a geologic event that resulted in the formation of a geologic material, expressed numerically and based on the results of a dating technique such as radiometric dating or dendrochronology. The value is an interpretation of the timing of that event rather than a direct, certain measurement of the specimen's age; it is conventionally termed absolute age, and also radiometric or apparent age.
terms.scopeNote: Conventionally termed absolute age, and also radiometric or apparent age. See GCDM section 6.4.

terms.label: Lower Temporal Boundary
terms.definition: The older (earlier) limit of an interval, the point in time at which the interval begins. By convention, older is "lower" (deeper in the stratigraphic column).
terms.scopeNote: By convention, older is 'lower' (deeper in the stratigraphic column).

terms.label: Radioactive Decay
terms.definition: The process where an unstable parent isotope loses particles from its atomic nucleus (decay) to form a daughter isotope (product) at a constant rate.

terms.label: Radiometric Age
terms.definition: Geologic age expressed in years determined by quantitatively measuring radioactive elements and their decay products.

terms.label: Radiometric Dating
terms.definition: Determination of a numeric (absolute) age by measuring the relative abundances of a radioactive parent isotope and its stable daughter product, together with the known decay constant, in a mineral or rock.

terms.label: Regional Timescale
terms.definition: A family of geologic timescales based on the strata and fossil record observed in a specific area, typically at the country or regional level.

terms.label: Relative Age
terms.definition: The geologic age of a fossil organism, rock, or geologic feature or event defined relative to other organisms, rocks, or features or events rather than in terms of years.

terms.label: Relative Dating
terms.definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

terms.label: Time Interval
terms.definition: A temporal entity with an extent or duration.

terms.label: Upper Temporal Boundary
terms.definition: The younger (later) limit of an interval, the point in time at which the interval ends. By convention, younger is "upper."
terms.scopeNote: By convention, younger is 'upper'.

terms.label: Feature
terms.definition: Abstraction of real-world phenomena.

terms.label: Feature of Interest
terms.definition: A feature of interest is an abstraction of a real-world phenomenon that is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling.

terms.label: Geologic Environment
terms.definition: Physical conditions found on the Earth's surface, which are determined by factors such as climate, tectonics, physiography, geography and within the Earth's interior, determined by pressure, temperature, chemical environment, and tectonics.

terms.label: Geologic Event Environment
terms.definition: The physical setting within which a Geologic Event takes place.

terms.label: Geologic Feature
terms.definition: A physical or conceptual feature that is hypothesized to exist coherently in the Earth and that results from geologic processes.

terms.label: Material Sample
terms.definition: A physical result of a sampling (or subsampling) event. Material samples are typically collected and either preserved or destructively processed.

terms.label: Petrographic Province
terms.definition: A broad area in which similar igneous rocks are formed during the same period of igneous activity.

terms.label: Physiographic Feature
terms.definition: A natural feature of the solid surface of the Earth or other planetary body.
terms.scopeNote: The manuscript cites 'FAO 2025' alongside INRAE 2021 for this definition; that citation is not resolved in the manuscript bibliography.

terms.label: Physiographic Province
terms.definition: A region in which all parts are similar in geologic structure and climate and which has consequently had a unified geomorphic history; a region whose pattern of relief features or landforms differs significantly from adjacent regions.

terms.label: Province
terms.definition: Any large area or region considered as a whole, all parts characterized by similar features or a history differing significantly from adjacent areas.

terms.label: Quarry
terms.definition: An open or surface mineral working, usually for extracting building stone, such as slate, limestone, etc. It is distinguished from a mine because a quarry usually is open at the top and front, and, in ordinary use of the term, by the character of the material extracted.

terms.label: Sample
terms.definition: A feature which is intended to be representative of a `FeatureOfInterest` on which `Observations` may be made.

terms.label: Sampling Event
terms.definition: An activity of Sampling carries out a (Sampling) Procedure to create or transform one or more Samples.

terms.label: Sampling Feature
terms.definition: The feature of interest a sample is intended to be representative of.

terms.label: Sampling Feature Type
terms.definition: The nature of the feature such as whether the feature is the result of natural processes.

terms.label: Sampling Location
terms.definition: The geographic place where a sampling event takes place.

terms.label: Tectonic Province
terms.definition: Groups of provinces linked by a common tectonic history are designated tectonic provinces. Tectonic provinces may contain a collection of sedimentary, igneous, structural, metamorphic, and metallogenic provinces.

terms.label: Tectonic Setting
terms.definition: A geologic event environment defined by relationships to tectonic plates on or in the Earth.

terms.label: Terrane
terms.definition: A fault-bounded area or region with different layers, rock structures, and geologic history from nearby areas that are not connected to them by unconformable contacts or changes in the rock's surface.

terms.label: Mine
terms.definition: A work for excavating minerals using pits, shafts, levels, tunnels, etc., as opposed to a quarry, where the whole excavation is open. In general, the existence of a mine is determined by the mode in which the mineral is obtained, not by its chemical or geologic character. The term also includes only excavations for their minerals or valuable mineral deposits.

terms.label: Division (Minerals)
terms.definition: The second rank of the Nickel–Strunz hierarchy, subdividing a class by a combination of chemical composition and crystal-structural type; encoded as the first letter of the Nickel–Strunz code. Equivalent to the IMA "subclass" level. E.g. within class 9 (silicates), division D = inosilicates (chain/ribbon silicates).
terms.source: Strunz & Nickel 2001, Mills et al. 2009, Wikidata Q396527
terms.scopeNote: In the Nickel–Strunz mineral classification, the rank immediately below class (the first letter of the code), subdividing a class by chemical composition together with crystal-structure type; termed 'subclass' in the IMA/CNMNC scheme.

terms.label: Type (Minerals)
terms.definition: In the Dana system, the rank below class and above group: a subdivision of a class based on more specific chemical/structural criteria — chiefly the cation-to-anion ratio and, in some classes, atomic structure. Encoded as the second number of the Dana number (quartz 75.1.3.1 → type 1).
terms.scopeNote: In the Dana system of mineralogy, the rank between class and group (the second element of the Dana number), subdividing a class by more specific chemical criteria such as the cation-to-anion ratio, and in some classes by atomic structure.

terms.label: Group (Minerals)
terms.definition: A mineral group consists of two or more minerals with the same or essentially the same structure, and composed of chemically similar elements.

terms.label: Structural Group
terms.definition: An informal descriptor for a set of minerals sharing essentially the same crystal structure (isostructural minerals). Under the standardized IMA/CNMNC nomenclature it is not a distinct rank; it corresponds to a formal group (isostructural species) or supergroup (isostructural groups). Historic usage such as "apatite structural group" has been replaced by formal frameworks — e.g. the apatite supergroup, subdivided into groups (Pasero et al. 2010), and the amphibole supergroup (Hawthorne et al. 2012).
terms.source: Mills et al. 2009, Pasero et al. 2010, Hawthorne et al. 2012
terms.scopeNote: Informal term for a set of minerals having essentially the same crystal structure (isostructural minerals). Not a formal rank in the IMA/CNMNC hierarchy, where such a set constitutes a mineral group, or a supergroup of structurally related groups.

terms.label: Species (Minerals)
terms.definition: The base unit of mineral classification: a naturally occurring mineral distinguished by a unique combination of characteristic chemical composition and distinct crystal structure. Two minerals are different species if they differ in either composition or structure. Species status is adjudicated by the IMA Commission on New Minerals, Nomenclature and Classification (CNMNC). Underlying definition of a mineral (Nickel 1995, verbatim): In general terms, a mineral is an element or a chemical compound that is normally crystalline and that has been formed as a result of geological processes.
terms.scopeNote: The fundamental unit of mineral classification: a naturally occurring substance, normally crystalline and formed by geological processes, distinguished by a unique combination of chemical composition and crystal structure, and recognized as a distinct species by the IMA/CNMNC.
